title: Dilucidationes super methodo elegantissima, qua illustris de la Grange usus est in integranda aequatione differentiali dx/√X = dy/√Y

deep.reconstruction:
Context (§§61–64). Euler is examining a degenerate ('paradoxical') case of Lagrange's method, with R = a+bx+cxx and S = a+by+cyy. The previous page gives p = x+y and an infinitesimal parameter α. Setting Δ = bb − αΓ leads to the integral (b+cp)² = Γ·RS, that is, RS/(b+cp)² = F (constant). The check below shows this is an integral of dx/R ± dy/S = 0 for a quadratic R, which suggests the degenerate case is the one where the quartic X is the perfect square R². I have not verified that from the earlier pages.

This page (§63–64). With u = xy, Euler writes
RS = aa + abp + ac(pp−2u) + bbu + bcpu + ccuu = (ap+bu)(cp+b) + (a−cu)².
Dividing by (cp+b) once gives F(cp+b) = ap + bu + (a−cu)²/(cp+b). Dividing again and using (ap+bu)/(cp+b) = a/c − (b/c)(a−cu)/(cp+b) gives
F = a/c − (b/c)V + V², where V = (a−cu)/(cp+b).
Since F is constant, V must be constant. The integral is therefore the symmetric bilinear (Möbius-type) relation (a − cxy)/(b + c(x+y)) = Const.
Check: for a = c = 1, b = 0, this is (1−xy)/(x+y) = cot(arctan x + arctan y), and F = 1 + V². This is correct for dx/(1+xx) + dy/(1+yy) = 0.
Euler then forms equivalent constants:
- a/c − (b/c)V = (ap+bu)/(b+cp).
- Dividing that by V gives (a(x+y) + bxy)/(a − cxy) = Const.
He says these agree with the forms of §24ff.

Theorem V (§65). This begins the general statement. Let Z = A+Bz+Czz+Dz³+Ez⁴ and let Π:z = ∫₀^z dz/√Z. Then Π:k = Π:x + Π:y holds exactly when
[2A + B(x+y) + 2Cxy + Dxy(x+y) + 2Exxyy ∓ 2√(XY)]/(x−y)² = (2A + Bk ∓ 2√(AK))/kk.
The proof on the next page fixes the constant Δ by putting y = 0, which forces x = k. This is Euler's addition theorem for elliptic integrals, restated in Lagrange's framework.
errors: Printed numerators read 'cxy + a(x+y)' and 'a(x+y) + cxy'; they should read 'bxy + a(x+y)' and 'a(x+y) + bxy'. Correct forms: (a(x+y)+bxy)/(b+c(x+y)) = Const and (a(x+y)+bxy)/(a−cxy) = Const. With c in place of b the expressions are not invariant: with a=c=1, b=0 the first becomes 1 + 1/p − K, which is not constant.
The instruction 'Subtrahamus utrinque a/b (a/o?)' does not match the computation as printed. The step that works is to take a/c − (b/c)V, equivalently F − V², which gives (ap+bu)/(b+cp).
The printed denominator 'cxy − a' differs only by sign from a − cxy, so this is harmless.

ideas.what: Resolving a degenerate case of Lagrange's method by an infinitesimal parameter (Δ = bb − αΓ), then reducing RS/(b+cp)² = Const to the bilinear invariant (a−cxy)/(b+c(x+y)) = Const by writing F as a quadratic in V
ideas.modern_name: Addition law for ∫dx/(quadratic): a Möbius/bilinear symmetric relation, i.e. the degenerate (genus-0) case of the elliptic addition theorem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (elementary addition formulas for arctan/log); degeneration within Lagrange's 1766-69 method
ideas.where_published: E506 itself (§§24ff. and here); Euler's addition-theorem papers E251, E252, E261, E345

ideas.what: Notation Π:z for ∫₀^z dz/√Z with a general quartic Z, and the addition theorem Π:k = Π:x + Π:y with an explicit symmetric algebraic relation
ideas.modern_name: Euler's addition theorem for elliptic integrals (general quartic)
ideas.where_published: E251, E252, E261, Institutiones calculi integralis I; restated here in E506

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine verification of a degenerate case plus a restatement of Euler's well-known addition theorem. The only finding is a printing or computational slip: cxy in place of bxy.
transcription_corrections: First display of §64: the numerator is printed as 'a − u' in the image (the c is missing); it should be a − cu.
'Subtrahamus vtrinque a/b' — the image reads 'a/o', probably a/c. Either way the step should be a/c − (b/c)V.
In 'F(cp+b) = ap + b'u + …' the stray apostrophe is a print artifact; read bu.
The footer 'zA+' is the catchword '2A+' for the next page.
